title: Set an adjustable walking pole to its owner's mark: open the flip lock, draw the shaft out to the red line, lock it
keywords: hold one section while sliding the other
instruction: Lengthen the walking pole until the red line on its shaft is at the edge of its upper clamp, lock it at that length, and let go of it.
context: Setting an adjustable walking or trekking pole to its owner's length is something most hikers and many older walkers do: open the flip lock, slide the shaft out to the mark on its printed scale, and snap the lever shut so the pole holds when leaned on. Black Diamond's pole instructions: "Hold the pole above the FlickLock to prevent the pole from rotating while pushing the cam lever open with your thumb", "Adjust pole to the desired length", "'Snap' close the lever firmly". The skill is a length adjustment against friction to a mark, then a cam lock that must hold load, not a twist or a click: the open collar still drags on the shaft (4 N) while the loose pole slides on the table at about 1.5 N, so one hand pulling the shaft only drags the whole pole; one hand holds the upper section above the clamp while the other opens the lever, draws the shaft out to the line and presses the lever shut. A half-closed lever slips under a lean.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. One adjustable walking pole (Black Diamond Trail Back class: 3-section aluminium, two flip-lock clamps, 100 to 140 cm, 267 g; sizes are estimates), loose, lying across the table along y at x 24, grip to the right (grip top at y -62), tip to the left (y +43), resting on its flat-sided grip (13 x 3 x 2.6 cm) and its upper clamp (2.5 cm across, black, y -3.5 to -0.5) with its axis 1.3 cm up. Upper shaft 18 mm, blue; middle shaft 16 mm, silver, with a printed scale (lines every 5 cm, 100 to 140 cm) read at the clamp's lower edge (y -0.5); the pole starts at 105 cm. A red paint-marker line marks 120 cm, 15 cm inside the upper shaft at the start; the maker's STOP line is at 140 cm. The upper clamp's lever (aluminium, 4.6 x 1.5 x 0.9 cm) is closed, lying on top of the clamp toward the grip. The lower clamp is closed at its setting and is not touched. Arms at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Length is grip top to tip. 0.4: the length has been within 1 cm of 120 cm (red line within 1 cm of the clamp edge). 0.7: locked at the mark: lever within 5 deg of flat, length within 1 cm. 1.0 (held 1 s): locked at the mark, released (both grippers 4 cm or more from the pole), still 1 s, then a load test passes: the pole is pushed together along its axis for 1 s and the shaft slips 2 mm or less with the lever still within 5 deg. 0 for the run once the pole falls below the table top or the shaft passes its STOP line (140 cm). Real trial: tape measure; photo of the lever; stand the pole on a bathroom scale and press the grip down to 15.3 kg (150 N) for 1 s, the red line moving 2 mm or less against the clamp edge (ruler). The simulated lean is 20 N (see fidelity).
reset_notes: Open the upper lever, slide the pole back to 105 cm on its scale, close the lever, and lay the pole along its tape marks (grip top and clamp) with the lever on top. Check the lever's holding with the scale test now and then; adjust its tension screw to the maker's setting if it slips. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz. The pole is one articulation: the middle section slides in the upper on a prismatic joint whose friction follows the lever (4 N open, rising to 250 N as it closes from 25 to 2 deg: estimates); the lever's pivot friction rises 0.06 to 0.20 N m (the cam). PhysX joint friction creeps under sustained load, so the sim's lean is 20 N, not the real 150 N. Grip flat-sided; strap and basket off.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; both grippers came down beside the pole near its clamp and hovered there; neither opened the lever or gripped the shaft, and the length stayed at 105 cm); demo: 1.0
